# Trump says all mines cleared from Strait of Hormuz

![](https://static.files.bbci.co.uk/bbcdotcom/web/20260817-125657-b933f830d3-web-3.18.0-12/grey-placeholder.png)
![Getty Images Trump, wearing a red MAGA cap, walks infront of the Marine Force One helicopter, and waves.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/news/480/cpsprodpb/0845/live/0d9a0730-9a52-11f1-aed2-8d6da8d75094.jpg.webp)

US President Donald Trump has said that the US Navy has removed or detonated all mines in the Strait of Hormuz - the vital waterway which Iran has largely closed since the beginning of the war in the Middle East.

"Iran has been notified that any ship or boat placing new mines will be immediately and systematically destroyed," Trump said in a post on his Truth Social platform.

There is no comment from Iran.

Closure of the strait has caused wild fluctuations in the price of oil on world markets. Trump has often said the US has control of the area - but Iran has fired against vessels it says have sought to cross without its permission.

Some 20% of the world's oil and liquefied natural gas used to transit the Strait of Hormuz before the war, which began on 28 February with US and Israeli air strikes against Iran.

In addition to closing the strait, Iran retaliated against Israel and against US bases in the region as well as US Arab allies in the Gulf.

A ceasefire aimed at facilitating talks to end the war has collapsed and there has been intermittent exchange of fire between the US and Iran.

For months, Ukraine fought a counteroffensive that almost nobody was allowed to see.

North of Lyman, in Donetsk Oblast, the 3rd Army Corps has been pushing Russian troops back around the village of Nove since May. There was so little geolocated video that analysts nearly missed it.

"The Ukrainians kept a good level of OPSEC and the Russians have been reluctant to publish videos from these areas," analyst Clément Molin noted in June, when the Russians were hiding their retreats.

The advance eases pressure on Sloviansk, one of the last free cities in eastern Ukraine, just 20 km to the southwest.

But the relief is partial. Russia is still grinding toward Sloviansk and Kramatorsk from several other directions, racing to close a pincer before winter strips the leaves and leaves any attacker exposed.
